findings.what: Self-hash tripwire with no regeneration path. `CoupledPreimageDirectRuntimeBindingV1.reopen()` reads the live `tac/witness_dsl/coupled_preimage_program.py` off disk and refuses unless its SHA-256 equals `DECODER_DIRECT_SOURCE_SHA256`, a constant stored INSIDE that same file. MEASURED today: live sha `4ed3ccc50f71be35577e69796cff89564151d6a4674772728b5f3c86d1f59b11` == the constant, so it passes right now. But `reopen()` is called unconditionally on the hot path at line 703 inside `consume_counted_coupled_preimage`, which means every consumption path in this module dies on ANY edit to `coupled_preimage_program.py` -- including a whitespace-only ruff reformat. Nothing in this file documents how to regenerate the constant. This is not hypothetical: the sister module `ep725_levelset_predictor_adapter.py` uses the same pattern and its pin is ALREADY STALE (see that file's critical finding).
findings.fix: Add a one-line comment at the DECODER_DIRECT_SOURCE_SHA256 definition naming the exact command that regenerates it, and add a repo check (or a preflight gate) that recomputes it, so the pin cannot silently rot the way ep725's did.

findings.what: `build_target_only_a_counterfactual` builds `baseline_payloads` and `counterfactual_payloads` as dicts keyed by `section.role` (lines 872-877). If a manifest ever carried two sections with the same role, the later one silently overwrites the earlier, and the 'non-target bytes unchanged' proof at lines 878-880 would skip a section without reporting it. Currently unreachable through the public entry points -- `_a_section` (line 633) and `_g_section` (line 640) both enforce exactly-one -- but this function accepts an arbitrary `baseline_sections` tuple and does not re-assert it.
findings.fix: Assert `len(baseline_payloads) == len(baseline_sections)` right after the dict comprehension, so a duplicate role becomes a typed error instead of a silently weakened proof.

findings.what: `AdaptedCoupledPreimagePairProgramV1.__post_init__` indexes `self.section_manifest[-1]` with no non-empty guard. findings.what: `MAX_ARCHIVE_OVERHEAD_BYTES = 1024 * 1024` guards `len(archive) > max_member_bytes + MAX_ARCHIVE_OVERHEAD_BYTES` at line 422. The real canonical overhead is 116 B (30 B local header + 5 B name + 46 B central header + 5 B name + 22 B EOCD, both names being '0.bin'), so the gate is ~9,000x looser than the format allows. With a small `max_member_bytes` the pre-parse size gate is effectively inert -- the real rejection happens later at line 328. Not a defect (deflate on incompressible data can expand, so some slack is required) but the constant is unexplained.
findings.fix: Either tighten to a derived bound (`116 + ceil(max_member_bytes * 0.001) + 64`) or add a comment stating that 1 MiB is deliberate slack and that line 328 is the real gate.

findings.what: ZIP framing audit came back CLEAN and I am recording the positive result, because this was the highest-cost bug class in the batch. Verified by hand against PKZIP APPNOTE: `_LOCAL_FILE_HEADER` '<IHHHHHIIIHH' = 30 B in exact field order; `_CENTRAL_DIRECTORY_HEADER` '<IHHHHHHIIIHHHHHII' = 46 B in exact field order; `_END_OF_CENTRAL_DIRECTORY` '<IHHHHIIH' = 22 B. `_build_exact_archive` pack order matches both headers field for field. Offset arithmetic closes exactly: central-directory start = 35 + compressed (line 174), central-directory size = 51 (line 194), archive length = 108 + compressed, and every one of those is independently re-derived and cross-checked by the parser at lines 265, 295-303, 357-359. Local-vs-central metadata is compared as a 9-tuple (lines 364-387). CRC-32 and decoded length are both re-verified (lines 394-397). Encode->decode byte-identity is measured by the test suite (16/16 pass) including a repeat-build determinism test. No section can be dropped or reordered: the archive is single-member by construction and the parser refuses `entries != 1` at line 263.

findings.what: Overlap detection audit came back CLEAN and I am recording the positive result. `SameClassRealizationRepairProgramV1.__post_init__` compares each run only against its immediate predecessor (lines 713-728), which looks like it could miss a non-adjacent overlap. It cannot. Runs are forced into `(pair_id, row, col_start, col_stop)` sorted order at line 711. For start-sorted intervals, if no consecutive pair overlaps then start_j >= stop_{j-1} for all j, which makes stop strictly increasing, which makes start_k >= stop_i for every k > i. So a consecutive-only check is sufficient. Wire ABI also verified: PACKET_HEADER '>8sBBHH32s32s32s32s32s32sIIII' = 222 B, RUN_ROW '>HHHHBBBBB' = 13 B, COMPOSITE_G_SECTION_HEADER '>8sBBHII32s32sII' = 92 B; CRC is computed over the header-with-crc-zeroed plus body on both encode (line 788) and parse (line 883), and the parse re-encodes and compares (line 924). Length accounting closes exactly at lines 862-865 and 302-306.
findings.fix: None.

This is safe here -- every dataclass is `frozen=True, slots=True` and every ndarray is copied and `setflags(write=False)` in `__post_init__` -- but the safety is load-bearing and undocumented. A future non-frozen field would leak state between tests.
findings.fix: One comment at the fixture noting that module scope is safe only because the surface is deeply immutable.

findings.what: Test quality audit came back STRONG and I am recording it. This suite would NOT survive replacing the implementation with canonical constants: `test_exact_falsifier...` (line 160) independently rebuilds the resize operator via `DisjointResizeOperator.build` and checks that post-repair scorer numerators equal `RGB * denominator` inside the owned mask and are bit-identical outside it (lines 214-226); `test_direct_decode_rejects_canonical_packet_with_wrong_live_g_class` (line 481) forges a CRC-valid packet through the module's own `_encode_packet` and proves the decoder still refuses on live-label disagreement; `test_deletion_body_mutation_and_trailing_bytes_fail_closed` (line 551) covers empty, truncated, bit-flipped and trailing-byte packets; `test_receipt_parser_rejects_numeric_and_truth_smuggling` (line 633) proves bool-as-int, float-as-int and truth-flag smuggling are all refused. The ABI assertions at lines 261-272 (222/13/62/9 bytes) are constants, but they pin the wire format, which is the correct thing to pin.
